items.creator: andy
items.box:
I want to give face the Files and the two Viewer, so i can examine the workings of fs-watcher and the generic viewers

- Files shell app (basically a shell-element)
- textViewer / launcher (becomes shell-element)
- mediaViewer (becomes shell-element)
- this include also the codeMirror display of text Files. (becomes shell-element)

- this time, i want to try the following: every table-row is a shell-element of type "file"

- there will be a shell element caller fileViewer, and two elements based on the fileViewer, the textViewer and the mediaViewer
- the fileViewer brings with it: annotationManager, and fStatViewer.

just a little preview of how this might be structured.
- A file element owns its value fields (name, size, changed, kind); a field that changes redraws only its cell.
- The file list is the standard list-tool, shell/js/probabilitySearch.js (goal/G30.17), given the file fields as its columns.

Challenges:
- making a list of file-elements look like a table with consistent cell-widths?
- having every fileElement listen for changes in it's size, or changes in it's associated fStat-element?

SETTLED
- Consistent cell widths: the list-tool is a table with declared columns (goal/G30.17).
- Each file row listens: fileElement holds one fs-watcher subscription for all rows and repaints only the changed cell (goal/G30.18).
- The text and media viewers move out of the old shell as shell elements (fileViewer, textViewer, mediaViewer); the old inline ones are deleted.
- On the face the mediaViewer plays as the pieces arrive: each sealed piece is opened as it comes and fed to the player. Formats that cannot start from their beginning alone (an MP4 whose index sits at its end) play once complete. The pieces stay in the viewer while it is open, so playing again plays from memory; closing the viewer drops them.
- The viewers keep what they do today, as elements: the title with the file name and Open for an app registered for its extension (the textViewer displays; editing stays the handler's, the textEditor app), the info bubble from fs.stat (fStatViewer), the annotations (annotationManager over fs.annotations and fs.annotate). CodeMirror loads when a textViewer first needs it, on the face as at home.
- The Files app's list is a probabilitySearch over fs.search with fileElement rows; fileSelector stays for the apps not yet ported.
- With no search words Files is a tree, every folder collapsed at first; pressing a folder opens or closes it. With words it is the ranked list.

THE FACELESS LAYER (the architecture all of this sits on)
- The shell is a transient version of the node: a faceless layer that mirrors the exact state of its node, and a UI that is a fast reading of that mirror. It runs and tests without a page.
- All data in one tree: data.files, data.contacts, data.preferences, one branch per type.
- Every stream event and every search answer becomes one of two writes: set(path, value) or delete(path), through one translator per event kind; nothing below is type-specific.
- Elements watch paths: watch(path, fn) is the only event handling; a write notifies the listeners of its path and of each path above it.
- A list is a view: a search ranks what the tree holds through a probability bucket made for that query; the node is asked only for what the tree cannot answer, and the answer is written into the tree.
- Files keeps what was good in the old Files: the mirror built from the stream, and one table that is a tree with the field empty and a ranked list with words.
- The faceless part of contacts is built here too (data.contacts), which the Your Node Home panel and the Contacts app both read.
- No cache bounding on the browser side: the node's file tree is unbounded too, and the page's copy is dropped on every refresh.
- One data cache, one stream: a page holds one stream to its node (the kernel shares it with every subscriber) and one data tree; nothing opens a second.
- The UI never waits on data: an app opens at once and directs what it gathers (Contacts opens and sends its empty search); data trickles in and the views redraw.

Read. What stands in the way today:

- The two viewers are not apps: they live inline in the old shell's index.html (text-file-launcher, the media viewer), and the face never loads that part.
- Files leans on the old shell: its file-type helpers (mimeTypeForName, classifyMimeType, CATEGORY) and the file selector, which reads the old shell's file tree.
- The text editor reads and writes its file synchronously, which the face cannot do.
- CodeMirror loads only when an app asks for it; the face has to fetch it on that first ask.

This fits the rule from G30.15: the file tree as an element fed by the fs-watcher stream, the viewers as elements of their own.

One question shapes the item: do the viewers move out of index.html into shell elements, used by the old shell and the face alike?
mote thoughts?

Thoughts, on your two challenges and around them:

- A table that is a list of elements: the list element owns one table and its columns; each file element draws its own row into it. The table keeps the widths consistent, and the rows stay separate elements. (A CSS grid where each row lays its cells into the parent's columns does the same, if a table feels wrong.)
- Every row listening for itself, without a thousand stream handlers: one dispatcher on the fs-watcher stream, keyed by path. A file element registers its path and hears only the events for that path. Each still listens itself; the lookup costs the same at 10 rows or 10,000.
- The stat is already on the stream: every fs-watcher event carries the path, the change, the size and when it changed. So the fStatViewer needs no request of its own; it is fed by the same event as its row.
- Rows come and go (search, scrolling), so every element needs a 'gone' step that drops its listener. The shell has no unmount today, and Contacts already works around that. A proper element lifecycle (mount, listen, leave) is the first piece to build.
- The annotationManager: annotations are read synchronously today. It needs an async read and, under your rule, should listen for annotation changes too.
- The face already gets the whole tree as fs-watcher commands at face-open, so Files on the face has its data from the first second.

The lifecycle and the dispatcher are what every later element stands on.

- A header press sorts by its field, a second press reverses.

One choice in the sorting: the list only holds what the search brought (the bucket, cut at one answer with 'more'). Sorting what is loaded is instant but can miss rows it doesn't have; asking the server to sort is complete but costs a round trip. Which, for a header press: sort what's loaded, or ask the server?

The standard shell list-tool: shell/js/probabilitySearch.js, a finished intrinsic shell element. Files and Contacts both use it. Apps not yet ported into the new shell keep using shell/shared/js/listSearch.js until none does; then it is deleted.

WHAT WE TAKE FROM shell/shared/js/listSearch.js
- Rows kept by key, every row any search brought, in one unbounded probability bucket; a later answer replaces a row with the same key.
- Ranking as you type: every row scored by probabilityStringObjectMatch against the words, times every filter's test; best on top.
- The matched letters marked in the row, and the match bar beside it.
- One call on the wire at a time, no typing pause; the latest words go the moment the answer returns.
- Filters declared by the app and drawn by the element, toggles included.

WHAT WE ADD
- A column mapping: which value field of a row goes in which column. It defines the column headers, and a header is a sort trigger.
- Column sort, client-side only, on the cached rows, combined with the filters; the server keeps no sort indexes.
- Search is row and data acquisition, with its filters; sorting is viewing the cached rows from different perspectives.
- No count line: the list says neither how many match nor that more exist.
- No cut-off: a search never stops where only zero-probability rows are left. Server-side above all, a server fills its bucket with all it has; the browser is better off with too much data than too little.

THE CONFIGURATION OBJECT
- api, server, verb: where the rows come from (the server searched, its stream, its search verb).
- args(text, filters): the verb's arguments.
- columns: [{ field, label, width, align, sort }]: the column mapping; sort says how a field compares (text, number or date). Replaces head and paint.
- element(row): optional, the shell element that draws a row when a row is more than its fields (a file, a contact).
- filters, matched(row, filters), score(row, filters), rows(), fold(row, key), empty: as in listSearch.
- Returns { refresh, redraw, words(), ask(verb, args), sort(field, direction), destroy }.

BEHAVIOUR, AND WHAT SHAPES IT
- The server's answers only feed the cache. While a search is out the words keep changing, so the server never knows the current words; what the list shows is always ranked from the cache against the words as they stand now.
- Text in the search field: column sort is off; the ranking orders the list (columns and filters say what is matched).
- The field empty: the cached rows stand in rows() order, or the order they came; a header press sorts by its column's field, a second press reverses; filters still apply.
- A change to a row's value field, heard on its server's stream, redraws that row's cells only.
- destroy drops every listener, so a list that leaves the screen leaves nothing behind.

items.title: Elements for a single file and a single contact
items.creator: claude-windows

DRAFT. Elements for a single file and a single contact: two rowElements (element groups), fileElement and contactElement, in shell/js/rows/ (shell/js/rows/fileElement.js, shell/js/rows/contactElement.js). They carry the listeners and painters a subject needs for real-time updates, wherever the element is used: a list row and a details panel show the same element, so nothing has to keep the two in sync.

They are rowElements, the complementary shell elements to probabilitySearch (goal/G30.17): the shape that is ideal for its rows. The family: fileElement and contactElement in this item; jobElement and goalElement later, out of scope here.

THE CONTRACT EVERY rowElement MEETS (this pair is its first; probabilitySearch knows only this shape)
- Made from one row of a search answer; a key; its fields in order; a listener on its subject; destroy.
- expandInfo: fetches what is too large for a row, when it is wanted: long text, descriptions, attached lists, fan-out data. A row and a details header use the element's fields; a details screen asks expandInfo for the rest.
- shell/js/rowElement.js holds what every row element shares, and fileElement and contactElement inherit from it: each hands in only its own subject, fields, stream and expandInfo. rowElement does the shared work once: paints each field into its cell, registers the one listener with the stream dispatcher, drops it on destroy, runs expandInfo and keeps its answer. Inheriting is plain: rowElement.create(parts) builds the element from the parts fileElement or contactElement hands in; no class chains.
- The stream dispatch lives per kind, in the element's own file: fileElement.js holds one stream subscription for all file rows and an index by path, contactElement.js one for all contact rows indexed by key. A row registers its subject there on create and leaves on destroy; rowElement only gives that register-and-leave helper. There is no separate dispatcher.
- A rowElement carries its actions (add, block, remove, open), so a row and a details screen offer the same ones.
- Fan-outs: an element may carry references to the elements that hang off its subject, such as a chatElement when the subject has a chat.

THE SHAPE OF A rowElement
- An item is a listener and its fields, in order:
  { listener, fields: [ { name, fieldRule, painter, editor } ] }
- listener: one per item (usually per row). It hears the stream events about its subject and hands each changed field to that field's painter; it is dropped when the item leaves the screen.
- fieldRule: the field's rule from js/fieldRules.js, the one definition both sides of the wire use (bytes, not characters). An editor checks it before taxing the wire.
- painter: draws the field's value. A changed field repaints only itself.
- editor (only where the value may be changed): asks the server for the change and never paints the result; the confirmed change, broadcast on the stream, repaints the field everywhere it is shown. Editors are for the item's details dialog; a list row usually shows its fields without them.

fileElement
- Subject: one file or folder, by its path.
- Fields: icon (by its kind and type), name, size, changed. Fed by the fs-watcher's events for that path, which carry the size and the time of change.

contactElement
- Subject: one contact, by its key.
- Fields: presence (the dot), status (owned, blocked, held), label (editable: the rename).
- Fed by the presence events for that key and the contact's own changes (a rename, a block).

IN A LIST
- probabilitySearch (goal/G30.17) takes an item's fields as its columns: the column mapping names the item's fields, and each cell is that field's painter.

items.title: Upgrade new shells contact application with probabilitySearch
items.creator: andy
items.box:
Contacts has one search, in two tiers, on the new list-tool: one probabilitySearch (goal/G30.17) with contactElement rows (goal/G30.18), in the local shell and on the face alike, since both run the one Contacts app.

THE TWO TIERS
- Tier one, at once: contact.search answers from the book and from the shadow (the peers this node has heard of, seenPeers) together, one row shape for both.
- Tier two, streamed: the same call starts a network search across the relays. Each result is written into the shadow and streamed to the shell as one row as it arrives.
- The node keeps one network search going at a time: a contact.search starts one only if none is in flight. Searches that come while it is out are answered from the book and the shadow at once, and start nothing.
- A late result is still a real peer: it joins the cache and the current words rank it. Results join every open Contacts list, local and face; each ranks them by its own words.
- The shadow is the node cache, the rows are the shell cache; each search starts from what the last one learned.

THE LIST
- One list, cached by key: a peer in the book and found on the network is one row, its name and status from the book, its presence from the network.
- One row of filters: all, my puppets, blocked, held, relays, and at its very end a network toggle. Off, the list shows the book (and this node's relays); on, it shows the peers found on the network as well. No separate all or book choice.
- Columns: presence, status, label; label sorts as text.
- Each row keeps itself current through contactElement: presence, status and renames repaint from the stream. Contacts own presence painting (contactsWatchPresence, contactsPaintPresence and their helpers) is deleted.
- A row in the book offers block, unblock and remove; a row found on the network offers Add (peer.acquire).
- Pressing a row opens it: Contact for a person, Relay Details for a relay.
- The list fills as soon as Contacts opens; an empty search answers like any other.

COMPONENTS REVISED
- Node, contact.search: answers book and shadow matches and starts the network search.
- Node, the network search: the relay walk now in peer.search runs as a job whose updates each carry one found row; contactElement subscribes to it like the other jobs.
- Node, peer.search: deleted, once nothing uses it.
- Desk onboarding: starts the network search job and reads its rows when the job says it is done, instead of asking peer.search.
- Join, its contact step: shows the same one Contacts list instead of peerFind.
- Face stream: carries the network search job and contact.rename, so the face repaints like the local shell.
- Shell, contactElement: the add action, and rows in and out of the book.
- Shell, Contacts: the book list and peerFind become the one list; peerFind is deleted.
- The suites that assert peer.search or peerFind are rewritten to the one list and the job.
- listSearch stays for the apps not yet ported.

THE INTERFACE CHANGE, APPROVED
- contact.search also searches the shadow and starts the network search.
- A new job kind, the network search, streamed to node and face.
- peer.search deleted.

THE NODE STORE SHEDS
- node.db never grows past 16 MB. Past it, the oldest packets of the packet log are deleted, in chunks, as new ones are written. The log is input to throw away, not a permanent record; the ruling of 2026-09-13 that it is permanent is overruled.
- The replay memory (hashes of packets received, so a replayed one is refused) keeps one day, not seven; a sealed packet older than a day is refused as old.
- The backlog a page is handed when it opens is the untaken packets of the last day, read through its index, never the whole log.
- Andy's store was cut by hand to the newest packets and the last week of replay memory (68 MB), the old file deleted.

items.title: create new face-app: mediaViewer
items.creator: andy
items.box:
A Media Viewer app, on the face as at home: pick a file, see or hear it.

THE APP
- shell/mediaViewer/, its own folder and manifest; its manifest says it runs at home and on the face, so the face shows its icon with no tag.
- Two shell elements and nothing of its own beside them: the files list element as a dropdown on top, the mediaViewer element under it, filtered to what it plays (images, sound, video).
- Picking a file shows it in the mediaViewer below; picking another drops the one before (its pieces freed).
- It opens at once and never waits on data: the dropdown fills as data.files does.

THE MEDIA VIEWER
- The mediaViewer element as built in goal/G30.16: at home the node streams the file to the player; on the face it plays as the sealed pieces arrive.

WHERE AN APP RUNS: ITS MANIFEST, AND NOTHING ELSE
- Every manifest, app or server, says where it runs: "runs": ["home", "face"], ["home"], or [] (off).
- The node starts and offers what says home; the face shows what says face.
- Both shells find their apps in data.files, the file tree already in the page: each shell/<app>/<app>.json there is read, and its runs decides. Nothing asks the node for a list of apps.
- The whole module include list is deleted: include.json, its reader (js/includeList.js), and the verbs config.setModules and config.searchModules. The config family stays, empty, for later use.
- Agent onboarding and offboarding (process/js/desk/onboard.js, offboard.js), which switched deskClient through that list, are deleted, with the four suites that built their world through them: agentOnboard, deskLoop, deskRedWriterBuild, publishData.
- Agent onboarding comes back later through a future "agent" server on Andy's own node, replacing deskAgent bit by bit, its good parts kept.
- The text viewer's include switch on a manifest is deleted; runs is edited in the text.
- Contacts, Files and Media Viewer run at home and on the face; the servers running today run at home; the rest [].
- A manifest is in git: switching an app off on one node is a local edit to a tracked file, and a pull can clash with it.
- A lab node starts every server whose manifest says home, so the slim default rests on the manifests in the tree.

ONE FOLDER PER OBJECT TYPE
- Shared, in shell/js: probabilitySearch.js (the list-tool, pane and dropdown), rowElement.js (the row base), spiritData.js (the one data tree, nothing type-specific).
- Each type in its own folder: shell/js/files/ and shell/js/contacts/, each with rowElement.js (its row), listElement.js (its drop-in list, pane or dropdown) and data.js (its translator: the stream events into set and delete on its branch: the fs-watcher for files; presence, renames and the network search for contacts).
- A new type is one new folder.
- The list-tool takes face: pane (open) or dropdown (closed, opening to the same list, closing on a pick, Escape or a press outside); the dropdown's mechanics are taken from the legacy listSearch and fileSelector.
- A list element takes a placeholder, a None button that picks nothing (its words the field's while nothing is chosen), and a pick(row, key); the list's value and row are the one picked.
- The intrinsic apps (Files, Contacts) are only mountable wrappers around these elements.

THE LEGACY SELECTORS GO
- Their users move onto the list elements in this item; shell/js/fileSelector.js is deleted with its api.ui.elements entry, and shell/js/contactSelector.js once its last user has moved.
- textEditor: the files list element as a dropdown, filtered to the text kinds, "open a file…" as its placeholder; a file found by its contents ranks by the node's contents score and opens at its line.
- grants: the contacts list element as a dropdown, "whose access…" as its placeholder and "all peers" as its None.
- introSpector: the contacts list element as a dropdown (relays are already in it), "self (this node)" as its None.
- chatter stays on the legacy contact selector for now: its rows carry each chat's state, and chats are likely a data type of their own, out of scope here. The contact selector is deleted when chatter moves.
